subject: Slot02: dominant opening delay precedes/complements shell reply; 8/10 cycles wait for coarse 90deg trigger
body: FIELD+SRC CONFIRMED at main bfbf5d68 / runtime f9ba2ca. Ten successful inner-wake calls have queueMs 0.257–1.267 (median 0.476) versus shellLatencyMs 154–202 (median 161). Physical inner ID was successfully primed at 05:32:49.275Z; first measured wake was 19.3 s later and all ten used the same physical ID, so the captured latency is not explained by a first-use physical-ID lookup. More important: only 2/10 cycles got a true DeviceState opening edge. In the other 8 cycles DeviceState changed 0->1 but Fold7DeviceStateObserver classified state 1 folded=true from the Android CLOSED physical-posture property; WakeInner was then delayed until a PUBLIC_STANDARD coarse 90deg sample. Delay from 0->1 to OPENING_FROM_CLOSED/WakeInner was 503–2486 ms, median 960.7 ms. In both true DeviceState edge cycles, INNER_HANDOFF preceded the wake Binder reply by 53.076 ms and 22.500 ms, proving shell receipt completion is not a state-machine gate. Those two cycles also had 67.565 ms and 83.158 ms gaps between cover-opening-visual END and INNER_HANDOFF. Current Fold7DeviceStateObserver, Fold7ContinuityController, ShizukuBridge.wakeInnerDisplay, DuoShellService wakeInnerPhysicalDisplay, and startup physical-ID priming are byte-identical to the 1.3.29 early-wake lineage, so do not assume the 166 ms receipt itself is a Gen4 code regression. AOSP Android 16 SurfaceFlinger setPowerMode schedules main-thread power work then waits for completion; instrument cacheHit/resolvePhysicalMs/surfacePowerCallMs and absolute invoke timestamps before changing behavior. Historical Slot01 should determine whether a later/earlier last-good build treated 0->1 differently. Do not change smooth close.
